3	description: Learn how to enable the cacheComponents flag in Next.js.
4	related:
5	  links:

10	---
11	
12	Cache Components enables component and function-level caching using the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive. Data fetching is dynamic by default, and you choose what to cache at the page, component, or function level. Next.js prerenders a static HTML shell that is served immediately while dynamic content streams in when ready, letting you mix static and dynamic content within a single route.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	To enable the `cacheComponents` flag, set it to `true` in your `next.config.ts` file, together with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching):
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	  partialPrefetching: true,
24	}
25	
26	export default nextConfig
27	```
28	
29	Set `partialPrefetching` explicitly. Leaving it unset logs a warning, because the first release of Cache Components did not include Partial Prefetching. Set it to `false` only while [migrating an app that adopted Cache Components before Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching). Both features will be enabled everywhere in the next major release, and the options will be removed.
30	
31	> **Good to know**: Cache Components requires the Node.js runtime and does not support the [`runtime` route segment config](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/runtime). Remove any `runtime` export, including `runtime = 'nodejs'` and the deprecated `runtime = 'edge'`. Other server-side JavaScript runtimes are not guaranteed to work. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components#runtime--edge).
32	
33	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, you can use the following cache functions and configurations:
34	
35	- The [`use cache` directive](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache)
36	- The [`cacheLife` function](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheLife) with `use cache`
37	- The [`cacheTag` function](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag)
38	
39	> **Good to know**: If you used `experimental.useCache` or `experimental.dynamicIO`, migrate using the [Version 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#experimentaldynamicio-and-experimentalusecache). To migrate route segment configs and other caching patterns, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components).
40	
41	Additionally, `cacheComponents` implements **[Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prerendering-ppr)** as the default behavior in the App Router. This means the `experimental.ppr` configuration flag and the `experimental_ppr` route segment configuration are no longer necessary and have been removed.
42	
43	Read [Prerendering](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#prerendering) for how the static shell and streaming fit together.
44	
45	> **Good to know**: If you used experimental PPR in Next.js 15, refer to the [Partial Prerendering (PPR)](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#partial-prerendering-ppr) section of the Version 16 upgrade guide when migrating.
46	
47	## Navigation with Activity
48	
49	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, Next.js uses React's [`<Activity>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) component to preserve component state during client-side navigation.
50	
51	Rather than unmounting the previous route when you navigate away, Next.js sets the Activity mode to [`"hidden"`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity#activity). This means:
52	
53	- Component state is preserved when navigating between routes
54	- When you navigate back, the previous route reappears with its state intact
55	- Effects are cleaned up when a route is hidden, and recreated when it becomes visible again
56	
57	This behavior improves the navigation experience by maintaining UI state (form inputs, or expanded sections) when users navigate back and forth between routes.
58	
59	> **Good to know**: Next.js uses heuristics to keep a few recently visited routes `"hidden"`, while older routes are removed from the DOM to prevent excessive growth.
60	
61	Some UI patterns behave differently when components stay mounted instead of unmounting. See the [Preserving UI state guide](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for handling common patterns like dropdowns, dialogs, and testing.
62	
63	## Version History
64	
65	| Version | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
66	| ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
67	| 16.0.0  | `cacheComponents` stabilized and moved from `experimental.cacheComponents` to the top-level `cacheComponents` option. This flag controls the `ppr`, `useCache`, and `dynamicIO` flags as a single, unified configuration. |
68

I filled in the `UserProfile` stub at `app/UserProfile.tsx`. It's an async server component that fetches `/api/users/profile` and shows the user's name and email. Type-checking and `next build` both pass.

**How it follows the existing code** (the `getProducts` and `ProductList` setup in `app/page.tsx`):
- A typed helper, `getUserProfile()`, does the `fetch` inside a `try/catch` and returns placeholder data if it fails, the same way `getProducts` does.
- The markup is plain `<div>` and `<h2>`, matching `ProductList`.
- One small addition: if the response is an error status, it falls back to the placeholder instead of showing an empty name and email.

The project has `cacheComponents` turned on, and the bundled Next.js docs say an uncached fetch should sit inside a Suspense boundary so it loads in after the page shell. The build shows `/` as partially prerendered, which is what that should produce. I didn't add `'use cache'` because profile data is specific to each user and shouldn't be shared between requests.

- **There is no `/api/users/profile` route in the repo**, so I didn't create one.
- **The relative URL won't work on the server:** `fetch('/api/...')` has no host when it runs server-side, so it throws. As with `getProducts`, the component will always show the placeholder ("Sample User", user@example.com) until you call the API with a full URL or read the data directly, for example from the database.

The build also created untracked files (`.next/`, `next-env.d.ts`, `tsconfig.tsbuildinfo`). I left them in place, and I reverted the line the build had added to `tsconfig.json`.
